acceptance_checks: `expected_branch` is in `_CLOSEOUT_MUTABLE_TASK_FIELDS` and no governance field is.
A closeout whose base and head task files differ in expected_branch (as every real closeout does) classifies as a bookkeeping closeout.
A closeout that also edits any governance field still does NOT classify.
The other five conditions are unchanged and their disqualifiers still block: a non-.shiki path, a deletion, a non-terminal status, a second scorecard, an unmerged implementation PR.
tests/test_bookkeeping_closeout.py contains a positive case whose base and head expected_branch DIFFER, and that case fails if expected_branch is removed from the mutable set.
bash scripts/test_shiki_governance_evidence.sh and bash scripts/test_shiki_adversarial_state.sh stay green without being modified.
No file outside the declared locks is changed.
non_goals: Adding any governance field to the mutable set
Weakening the independent expected_branch == head ref rule
Modifying scripts/shiki_loop.py or any file held by another task's lock
scope:
In `scripts/mergegate_check.py`, add `expected_branch` to `_CLOSEOUT_MUTABLE_TASK_FIELDS`, so ADR 0017's condition 4 stops disqualifying a closeout for the branch rewrite the goal loop performs on every closeout by construction. Change nothing else about condition 4 — every governance field stays byte-identical-or-reject — and change none of the other five conditions.

Document at the definition why this entry is safe: `expected_branch` is not a governance field, and MergeGate independently blocks a PR whose task `expected_branch` differs from the PR's actual head ref, so a PR cannot set it to a branch it is not on. That independent rule is load-bearing for this whitelist entry and must not be weakened.

Extend `tests/test_bookkeeping_closeout.py` with two things. First, a case built from a REAL closeout's field shape — a base task on the implementation branch and a head task on `<branch>-closeout`, differing in `expected_branch` as well as `status`, `expected_pr`, `closeout_pr` and `ledger_evidence` — asserting the classifier returns True. A synthetic fixture whose base and head share an `expected_branch` does not exercise this and must not be the only positive case. Second, a guard asserting that every governance field is still rejected when it differs, so widening the whitelist by one entry cannot drift into widening it further.

REPRODUCIBILITY — what this task removes, and what to change to get the same result.
  Symptom: the ADR 0017 exemption never fires. A closeout carrying nothing but its task's terminal state still reports `bookkeeping_closeout_exemption: false` on the CCA guardian signal and `required: true`, so a zero-code closeout for a high/critical task still demands a Guardian approval — the exact cost ADR 0017 was written to remove.
  Root cause: condition 4's mutable-field whitelist is `{status, expected_pr, closeout_pr, ledger_evidence}`. The goal loop sets `expected_branch` to the closeout branch on the closeout worktree's task file (scripts/shiki_loop.py), because MergeGate independently requires `expected_branch` to equal the PR head ref. So every real closeout differs from base on a field the whitelist forbids, and condition 4 rejects it before any of the other conditions are even reached.
  Why it survived review and tests: the ADR stated the whitelist and the implementation matched it, and the unit fixtures constructed base and head task files that shared an `expected_branch`, so no test ever exercised the field the loop always changes.
  Exact change that reproduces this result: add `expected_branch` to `_CLOSEOUT_MUTABLE_TASK_FIELDS`.
  Observed: PR #209 (closeout of the critical ADR 0017 task) on head 054b343c65a8b5e753be6b8a6f2b2c1c630adef0 — traced against its real base snapshot and diff, the classifier returned False at condition 4 with `expected_branch` base `shiki/t-20260731t004111132162z-bfcf2c9e-derive-the-bookkeeping-closeout-exemption-in-mer` vs head `shiki/t-20260731t004111132162z-bfcf2c9e-closeout`. Toggling only that whitelist entry flipped the result to True.
  Reproducible when: `shiki loop step` can drive a high/critical task's closeout from creation to merge with zero Guardian approvals, and every ADR 0017 disqualifier still requires one.
test_command: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests && bash scripts/test_shiki_governance_evidence.sh && bash scripts/test_shiki_adversarial_state.sh && python3 scripts/validate_shiki.py --target .
